# Missing-variant handling by assay class

Product requirement: what response an absent PGS-model variant gets, as
a function of the file\'s classified assay class (INTAKE-1: genotyping
array / gVCF / WGS / WES). Impute-first policy. Self-contained; every
threshold carries its citation and a provenance tag inline. Generated
2026-07-15.

::: legend
[SOURCE]{.t .s}stated directly by a cited source [INFERENCE]{.t .i}our
reasoning from the cited pieces; extrapolates past what any one source
states [NOT ESTABLISHED]{.t .n}the literature does not answer this ---
carried as an explicit gap
:::

## 1. The shared machinery (assay-independent)

Two thresholds do most of the deciding, both citable defaults rather
than choices:

- **Per-variant imputation quality** --- keep an imputed dosage if
  **INFO / R² / Rsq ≥ 0.3** (permissive default), tightened to **0.8**
  when stringent. [SOURCE]{.t .s}
  [\[R2\]](https://imputationserver.readthedocs.io/en/latest/pgs/getting-started/)
  [\[R3\]](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae331)
  [\[R4\]](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13073-020-00801-x)
- **Aggregate match rate** --- the PGS Catalog\'s own calculator refuses
  to report when the fraction of the scoring file\'s variants matched in
  the target falls below `--min_overlap`, **default 0.75**. [SOURCE]{.t
  .s}
  [\[R1\]](https://pgsc-calc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/explanation/match.html)

The four responses map onto these: **impute** (recover an unmeasured
site from an ancestry-matched panel, keep if INFO≥threshold);
**score-as-reference** (assign dosage 0 *only given positive hom-ref
evidence*); **drop** (exclude one unmatched variant from the sum);
**refuse** (decline the whole score on low aggregate coverage). The
impute-vs-score-as-reference split IS the \"absence means different
things per assay\" distinction: score-as-reference requires positive
evidence of a hom-ref call; imputation is what you do when absence means
\"not measured.\" [INFERENCE]{.t .i} (framing; the pieces are sourced)

Silently treating an *unmeasured* missing variant as reference biases
the score downward, proportional to the variant\'s weight and allele
frequency; the effect of a weighted score depends critically on the
availability of its large-weight variants. [SOURCE]{.t .s}
[\[R10\]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6053141/)

## 3. The WGS row, made measurable

The WGS response is not a risk-tolerance preference --- it is set by
three measured quantities.

### 3a. Callable fraction at 30×

**Genome-wide (measured):** at 30--40×, \~84% of an individual genome is
confidently sequenced and \~95% is covered at ≥10×; clinical-WGS SNP
sensitivity plateaus by \~20×. [SOURCE]{.t .s}
[\[R11\]](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1613365113)
[\[R12\]](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-021-00948-5) **Over PGS
positions:** PGS/GWAS variants are common and preferentially
well-mappable, and common-variant recovery is near-ceiling (\~86--97%
well-imputed for MAF\>0.05), so the callable fraction over PGS positions
is plausibly higher --- 95--99% at 30×. That per-PGS-position fraction
is **not directly measured** in any one source (Gap 1). [INFERENCE]{.t
.i} [\[R13\]](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3176314/)
[\[R5\]](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-022-22215-y)

### 3b. Residual assume-reference bias, by depth

Two error sources behave differently. **Within callable sites** the only
error is het-dropout: a true heterozygote read as hom-ref because every
read happened to be reference, probability `0.5^DP` per covered site
(first-principles binomial, ignoring base/mapping error --- not a
literature value). [INFERENCE]{.t .i} [\[R19\]](#derivation) At the
DP≥10 callable floor this is under 0.1% per site --- negligible in
aggregate. **Across the uncallable remainder** the error is
one-directional downward (`weight × 2 × effect-allele-freq` per
unmeasured site); direction and weight-dependence are established, but
the magnitude at a small (1--5%) remainder is extrapolation past the
published 20--70% range (Gap 4). [SOURCE]{.t .s}
[\[R10\]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6053141/)

::: {style="display:flex;gap:24px;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:flex-start"}

at DP 5, 0.098% at DP 10, \~1×10⁻⁴% at DP 20. The shaded band (≤5×) is

  Per-site DP   P(het→hom-ref)

### 3c. Depth at which assume-reference stops being defensible

Set by **per-site DP**, not the genome mean:

1.  **DP ≥ 10 --- defensible.** Het-dropout \< 0.1%; the conventional
    callable floor (ACMG 90--95% breadth above 10×; mosdepth default
    CALLABLE bin `5..149`). Pair with GQ ≥ 20 as the
    reference-confidence gate (GQ cutoff is convention --- Gap 2).
    [SOURCE]{.t .s}
    [\[R12\]](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12920-021-00948-5)
    [\[R16\]](https://github.com/brentp/mosdepth)
    [\[R6\]](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-38346-0)
2.  **DP \~5--8 --- marginal → impute.** Het-dropout climbs from \~0.4%
    to \~3%; no longer safe for a heterozygous carrier. [INFERENCE]{.t
    .i} [\[R19\]](#derivation)
3.  **Mean ≤ 5× (esp. \<1×) --- indefensible → impute.** At 1×, \~half
    of genotypes reflect only one of the two alleles, so
    assume-reference systematically miscalls carriers --- yet imputation
    rescues the same data (PRS accuracy at effective coverage ≥ \~0.5×;
    low-pass MSE far below array only via imputation). [SOURCE]{.t .s}
    [\[R14\]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8015847/)
    [\[R15\]](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6880438/)

### 3d. Variant-only VCF with no coverage track (the trap)

A 30× WGS delivered as a plain variant-only VCF **does not license
assume-reference at any depth**: the file cannot distinguish
callable-hom-ref from no-coverage, and the 30× genome mean says nothing
about per-site DP at a specific absent PGS position. Either obtain
per-site coverage evidence (companion gVCF or callable BED) or impute
the absent sites. **The deciding quantity is per-site DP read from a
coverage track --- never the genome-average depth.** [SOURCE]{.t .s}
[\[R7\]](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360035531812-GVCF-Genomic-Variant-Call-Format)
[\[R8\]](https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360035531532-HaplotypeCaller-Reference-Confidence-Model-GVCF-mode)
[\[R9\]](https://github.com/uclahs-cds/package-ApplyPolygenicScore/discussions/17)

**WGS row resolved:** with per-site coverage evidence ---
**score-as-reference** over the DP≥10 callable majority (known error
\<0.1%/site), **impute** the small remainder (INFO≥0.3, near-ceiling
recovery for common PGS SNPs), **drop** only sites both uncallable and
unimputable, **refuse** only if callable+imputed fraction \<0.75 or a
disproportionately high-weight variant is left unresolved. Without a
coverage track --- impute the absent sites; assume-reference is not
licensed.

## 4. Open gaps --- not established in the retrieved literature

::: gap
### Gap 1 --- Callable fraction over PGS positions specifically [NOT ESTABLISHED]{.t .n}

Genome-wide numbers are measured (30--40× WGS: 84% of an individual
genome confidently sequenced, \~95% covered ≥10×; clinical-WGS SNP
sensitivity plateaus by \~20× \[R11\]\[R12\]). PGS/GWAS variants are
common and sit preferentially in the well-mappable fraction, and
common-variant recovery is near-ceiling (well-imputed proportion
\~86--97% for MAF\>0.05 \[R13\]\[R5\]), so the callable fraction
restricted to PGS positions is plausibly 95--99% at 30×. But that
fraction has not been measured directly over PGS SNP positions in a
single source. The 95--99% figure is a well-supported INFERENCE, not a
cited fact.
:::

::: gap
### Gap 2 --- GQ ≥ 20 score-as-reference cutoff [NOT ESTABLISHED]{.t .n}

DP ≥ 10 as a reliability floor is defensible from the deep-WGS accuracy
literature \[R6\] and the ACMG 90--95%-breadth-above-10× guidance
\[R12\]. The exact GQ ≥ 20 pairing used to gate the score-as-reference
decision is genotype-filtering convention, not an identifier traceable
to a primary PRS source. Record it as a tunable default.
:::

::: gap
### Gap 3 --- WES imputation quality for the non-coding PRS backbone [NOT ESTABLISHED]{.t .n}

Whether off-target WES reads plus imputation can clear the 0.75
match-rate bar for a genome-wide model --- and at what INFO threshold
--- is unquantified in the retrieved literature. Highest-value item to
measure before the product reports WES-derived scores.
:::

::: gap
### Gap 4 --- Residual assume-reference bias at a small (1--5%) missing fraction [NOT ESTABLISHED]{.t .n}

The one simulation that quantifies missing-SNP bias \[R10\] tests a
missing fraction of 20--70% (correlation with the full GRS stayed \>0.8
at 20% missing). Extrapolating that curve down to a 1--5% uncallable
remainder --- where the deficit is essentially negligible --- is
INFERENCE past the published range. Direction (downward) and
weight-dependence ARE established; the small-remainder magnitude is not
a measured point.
:::

Provenance note: every reference R1--R18 was returned as a hit by a
literature/web search during preparation and its URL traced back to
those returned results; R19 is a labeled first-principles derivation,
not a citation. Author names are given only where the retrieved source
record carried them --- several records returned title + venue only and
are cited that way. Verification depth differs by reference: the
specific quoted *figures* from R11 (PNAS, 30--40× genome coverage) and
R12 (BMC Med Genomics, clinical-WGS sensitivity / ACMG 10× guidance)
were checked against the retrieved snippet text; the remaining
references are traced as returned search results, and the exact numbers
attributed to them should be confirmed against the source page before
the manuscript relies on them. No version pinning --- the product
records API/tool versions at run time.
